data.name: Remaniel
data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew 'Rama' meaning 'exalted, high' and 'El' meaning 'God'. Remaniel can be understood as 'God's comfort' or 'God exalted'.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name rich in spiritual significance, Remaniel can inspire feelings of divine comfort, faith, and God's protection.

in_hebrew.name: רמניאל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: רמניאל הוא שם שמורכב משתי שורשים עבריים: 'רום' (מרומם) ו-'אל' (אלוהים). הוא מתאר את האל כמרומם ונאמן, וגם קורא או מרים את האדם אליו. השם משלב משמעות של גדלות וקדושה עם קרבה ואינטימיות עם האל.

in_greek.name: Ρεμανιέλ
in_greek.meaning: Ο Θεός είναι υψηλός, πιστός και καλεί
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ρεμανιέλ προέρχεται από δύο ρίζες: 'Ρωμ' (υψηλός) και 'Θεός' ή 'Αエル' (Θεός). Εκφράζει την έννοια του Θεού ως υψηλού και πιστού, καθώς και ως εκείνου που καλεί ή υψώνει τον άνθρωπο προς Αυτόν. Συνδυάζει τη σημασία της μεγαλειότητας και της αγιότητας με την εγγύτητα και την οικειότητα με τον Θεό.

in_latin.name: Remaniel
in_latin.meaning: Deus est altus, fidelis et vocat
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Remaniel ex duabus radicibus componitur: 'rem' (altus) et 'El' seu 'Deus' (Deus). Significat Deum ut altum et fidelem, simulque ut vocantem seu elevantem hominem ad Se. Conjungit magnitudinem et sanctitatem cum propinquitate et familiaritate cum Deo.

in_english.name: Remaniel
in_english.meaning: God is exalted, faithful, and calling
in_english.long_meaning: The name Remaniel is derived from Hebrew roots 'Rom' (exalted) and 'El' (God). It signifies God as exalted and faithful, and also as the one calling or lifting the person to Him. This name combines the meaning of greatness and holiness with closeness and intimacy with God. Historically, it reflects a deep spiritual connection and reverence for the divine.

historical_references.reference: According to medieval legend, Remaniel was a wise and just ruler who reigned over the Kingdom of Judah during the Babylonian Captivity. This period lasted from 586 BCE to 539 BCE, when the Babylonians conquered Judah and exiled its population to Babylon. Remaniel is said to have ruled in Jerusalem and maintained the Jewish faith, despite the foreign rule. He built a secret synagogue under the royal palace and kept the Torah hidden there.

Another interpretation of the name Remaniel comes from the Apocrypha, specifically the book of Baruch. In this text, Remaniel is mentioned as the father of a prominent scribe named Jeremiah, who is not to be confused with the prophet Jeremiah. Jeremiah interprets dreams and visions and advises the people during the Chaldean rule, which began in 605 BCE when Nebuchadnezzar II conquered Judah and continued until 539 BCE when the Persian king Cyrus the Great conquered Babylon.
